clue.text: Caught fungal infection scratching backside, with your pen essentially inserted — that's embarrassing

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the middle of pen is put inside the trimmed infection
scratching out the back end of the infection's name removes its last letter

parts.note: ringworm is a fungal skin infection

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter, here of pen

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A patient with an itchy fungal complaint, scratched with a pen, finds the whole business mortifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching backside' cuts RINGWORM to RINGWOR; 'inserted' puts E, the core of 'pen', inside to give RINGEWOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes you wince with shame is excruciatingly awkward, the colloquial sense of embarrassing.

clue.text: That girl in school is stuck

indicators.note: the pronoun is placed in the middle of the school word

parts.note: a coed is a co-educational school
her refers to that girl

explanation.surface: A report that some girl at school has got stuck somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together, so the past tense matches having stuck together.

clue.text: Suggest, in a feeble manner, going topless

indicators.note: losing its top removes the first letter of the adverb in a down entry

parts.note: limply means weakly, in a feeble manner

explanation.surface: A coy hint that someone half-heartedly took their top off.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to hint at or insinuate it without stating it.

clue.text: Organised criminal is impressive

indicators.note: criminal letters are bent or wrong, so the word Organised is rearranged

explanation.surface: Organised crime as an impressive operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like the anagram signal for 'criminal', but it is the reverse: 'criminal' signals rearranging ORGANISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose means imposing or magnificent in scale, a close sense of impressive.

clue.text: River sport

definitions.meaning: a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham
to sport an item of clothing is to have it on

explanation.surface: Two words suggesting a day of watersports.
explanation.definitionFit: The Durham river shares its name with the verb for having clothes on, as in sporting a hat.

clue.text: Endures river that is flooding Oxford University

indicators.note: the Latin phrase flows around the university abbreviation, as flood water surrounds a place

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Oxford weathers a river bursting its banks into the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' gives the Latin id est, not the usual IE abbreviation; 'flooding' wraps it around the university.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride out a storm is to survive it to the end, an idiom for weathering or enduring.

clue.text: Leading man's new bird

parts.note: the hero is the leading man of a story

explanation.surface: A film's star has a new girlfriend, bird being slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Male animal in discomfort beginning to emit unpleasant chemical

indicators.note: the male animal sits within the word for discomfort

parts.note: pain is discomfort
a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: the beginning of emit is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An animal in distress starts to give off a nasty substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are foul-smelling compounds formed when protein decays, once blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Dessert in Finland mostly served up with peel of star-apple

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the trimmed name is read upwards
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: Suomi is the Finnish name for Finland

indicators.note: the peel is the outside, so the first and last letters of star-apple

explanation.surface: A Finnish pudding served with the skin of an exotic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims SUOMI to SUOM; 'served up' turns it to MOUS; 'peel of' gives S and E from star-apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped sweet dish, often chocolate, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Disorganised figure taking clothes off has problem

indicators.note: stripping off the outer letters leaves the inside of the word

parts.note: a figure is a shape
a hazard is a danger or problem

explanation.surface: A naked figure has a problem on their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking clothes off' strips S and E from SHAPE, leaving HAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means random and lacking any plan, so it fits chaotic, disorganised work.

clue.text: Old-fashioned doorman powerless, on reflection

indicators.note: seen in a mirror, the trimmed word is read backwards
without P, the physics symbol for power

parts.note: a porter keeps the door of a hotel or college

explanation.surface: A doorman, thinking it over, is an old-fashioned figure with no power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerless' takes P from PORTER, leaving ORTER; 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes styles deliberately imitating those of an earlier era.

clue.text: As part of Commonwealth day I ran around city

indicators.note: the hidden run is turned around, read backwards
the letters are part of the phrase Commonwealth day I ran

explanation.surface: A runner describes jogging laps for Commonwealth Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As part of' hides HDAYIR in 'CommonwealtH DAY I Ran'; 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Titillating at first, star novelist makes waves

indicators.note: the opening letter of Titillating

parts.note: the Sun is a star
Kingsley or Martin Amis, English novelists

explanation.surface: A writer begins with racy material and causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes waves' looks like the idiom for causing trouble; 'makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are huge sea waves set off by undersea earthquakes.

clue.text: Medic in court blocking entrance

indicators.note: the court abbreviation sits in the doorway, blocking it

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A doctor appears in court while someone stands in the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic is a physician, a qualified medical practitioner.

clue.text: Cold meat pie with no base concerning Victor

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ham is a meat

indicators.note: in a down entry the base is the bottom letter, which is removed

parts.note: on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A cold meat pie without its pastry bottom, apparently about a man called Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no base' trims PIE to PI. 'Victor' looks like a man's name, but it means a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is a winner, someone who has beaten all rivals.

clue.text: Make pleasant smell with fragrant plant

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
anise is an aromatic herb tasting of liquorice

explanation.surface: Using a fragrant herb to freshen up a smelly room.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: To humanise is to make kinder or more civilised, a loose sense of making pleasant.

clue.text: Love how much fuss one can receive?

definitions.text: how much fuss one can receive?
definitions.meaning: read cryptically as an ..., the allowance of fuss one person gets

explanation.surface: A wry question about how much fussing a loved one can take.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into ADO (fuss) and RATION (an allowance); the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is worshipful affection, a stronger synonym of love.

clue.text: Wooden panelling was hemming in bed

indicators.note: the word was surrounds the word in, as a hem encloses an edge

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Panelling once boxed in a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is oak panelling lining the lower walls of a room.

clue.text: is caused by my repeated depression and "Special One" going to pub

definitions.text: is caused by my repeated depression

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: The 'Special One', Jose Mourinho's nickname, drowns his sorrows in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens on a blank before 'is': the definition is that gap, made by the setter pressing the key repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Each press of this long keyboard key puts a blank between words, like the gap opening the clue.

clue.text: Evacuated station with long grass

indicators.note: emptying the word station leaves only its outside letters

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A deserted railway station overgrown with tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is not a plant here but slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass and snitch are both slang for an informer who tells on others.

clue.text: Effective place to wee when camping?

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
campers sleep in a tent

explanation.surface: A camper wonders where to relieve themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is an informal British word for a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Potent means powerful and producing a strong result.

clue.text: Bores head back north and get lost regularly

indicators.note: in this down entry the word for head is read backwards

parts.note: nut is slang for head

indicators.note: taking every other letter of get lost

explanation.surface: Someone is told to turn north and clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns NUT to TUN; 'regularly' takes E, L and S from 'get lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bores as a verb means drills holes, as tunnels are dug through rock.

clue.text: Forward unwise to ignore introduction from referee

indicators.note: the letter is ignored, left out of the longer word

parts.note: imprudent means unwise

indicators.note: the opening letter of referee

explanation.surface: A football forward rashly disregards the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a football position but means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of presumptuous or cheeky matches being disrespectfully bold.

clue.text: Gloomy daughter's back

parts.note: the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A daughter's back is giving her a miserable time.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal.

clue.text: Dotty over young woman

definitions.meaning: in cricket an over with no runs scored is all dot balls on the scorecard
an old word for an unmarried girl

explanation.surface: Someone is mad about a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty over' reads as smitten with, but in cricket a scoreless over is recorded as six dots.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over without a run and an old word for a young unmarried girl share one name.

clue.text: Artist to prepare air-free environment?

definitions.meaning: to remove the gas from something

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a vacuum.
explanation.definitionFit: The French painter of ballet dancers shares a spelling with a verb for clearing out the gas.

clue.text: Sticks up for superior

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom

parts.note: gums means sticks with glue

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for a superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug and superior both describe self-satisfied looking down on others.

clue.text: K Cobain's widow provides spice

definitions.meaning: Courtney Love, widow of Kurt Cobain, styled by initial and surname as he is
a dried flower bud used as a spice

explanation.surface: A rock widow branches out into selling spices.
explanation.walkthrough: As 'K Cobain' is initial plus surname, so is his widow, Courtney Love.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock widow's initial and surname spell the name of a pungent dried bud used in cooking.

clue.text: On my way to drink drop of malt — the French blend

indicators.note: the word for on my way swallows the letter

parts.note: I'm coming means I'm on my way

indicators.note: a drop is just a little, the first letter of malt

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Heading off to the pub to sip a malt whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: To commingle is to mix together, a synonym of blend.

clue.text: Patriot's song upset supporters

indicators.note: letters upset are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fans are angered by a national anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: Protagonists can mean champions or advocates of a cause, so supporters.
